spots.name: Gulf State Park Campground (primitive tent loop)
spots.priceNote: $25/night primitive tent-only sites 501-508 (tent pad, fire pit, table; no hookups) + reservation fee/taxes; full-hookup sites run $50-90+
spots.locationNote: In Gulf Shores, ~2 mi north of the beach road; ~17-18 route miles BEFORE the Day 1 endpoint (shorten the day)
spots.legalityNote: Alabama state park; tents welcome on all 496 sites plus the 8 primitive tent-only sites
spots.cyclistIntel: The route threads Gulf State Park's paved Backcountry Trail system, so the campground is essentially on-route; common first/last Alabama night for Southern Tier riders
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; post-Labor Day availability is good

spots.name: Southport Campground
spots.priceNote: Tent/primitive sites offered per Gulf Shores tourism listing; current tent rate unpublished (est. $25-35, RV sites ~$40s) — call to confirm; website was unreachable Aug 2026
spots.locationNote: Under the Intracoastal Waterway bridge on the north edge of Gulf Shores, ~12 mi before endpoint
spots.legalityNote: Established private campground advertising RV and tent camping with hot showers and clean restrooms
spots.cyclistIntel: No specific touring-cyclist reports found; nearby Doc's RV (mi 68.6) is explicitly NO tents and Island Retreat is $64+/RV-focused, so this is the tent-friendly pick of the mile-66-69 cluster
spots.seasonalNote: Open all year

spots.name: Fort Morgan RV Park
spots.priceNote: Tents allowed per Good Sam/Hipcamp listings but rates not published (RV full-hookup sites listed 'from $93' on Hipcamp; likely $50+ for any site) — call and ask for a one-night tent-camper rate
spots.locationNote: 10397 2nd St on Bon Secour Bay, ~1 mi from the Fort Morgan ferry landing — only camping within striking distance of the 8:00 AM boat
spots.legalityNote: Established 34-site private park; listings say 'tent campers, car campers, pop-ups welcome'
spots.cyclistIntel: Strategic rather than cheap: camping here guarantees the 8:00 AM ferry. Fort Morgan historic site itself has no camping
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round

spots.name: Dauphin Island Campground
spots.priceNote: $22/night tent (year-round) + 5% maintenance fee + 11% lodging tax = ~$25.60 total; reservations require a 2-night non-refundable deposit, so walk-up as-available is simpler for one night
spots.locationNote: On Dauphin Island, ~0.5 mi from the Mobile Bay Ferry landing and Fort Gaines; requires crossing the bay (last ferry from Fort Morgan 3:30 PM)
spots.legalityNote: Town-run 151-site public campground; fully legal, tent sites back onto the Audubon Bird Sanctuary
spots.cyclistIntel: Classic Southern Tier stop — riders roll off the ferry straight into the campground; island is very bike-friendly. Tent sites have water/electric. Gate house open 7 AM-6:30 PM (7 PM Fri/Sat)
spots.seasonalNote: Sept is 'winter season' rate period; late Sept is peak hurricane season — ferry suspends in winds >35 mph, have a bail-out plan

spots.name: Shepard State Park (primitive tent areas)
spots.priceNote: Primitive tent camping $13/night (3 first-come areas, 3-day max); developed W/E sites historically $18 but a Feb 2025 camper reported $38 ($33 senior/military) — confirm primitive rate by phone
spots.locationNote: 1034 Graveline Rd, Gautier — ~5 route miles past Pascagoula, ~1 mi off US 90
spots.legalityNote: State park (city-operated); primitive tent camping explicitly 'allowed and encouraged'
spots.cyclistIntel: Long-running budget stop for Southern Tier riders along the MS coast; restrooms/bathhouses on site, quiet pine woods
spots.seasonalNote: Open; park website advises checking operating status before arrival (phone lines were down mid-2026)

spots.name: Davis Bayou Campground (Gulf Islands National Seashore)
spots.priceNote: NPS campground (type approximated): $20 standard non-electric / $22 electric per night via recreation.gov; 50% off with federal Senior/Access pass
spots.locationNote: 3500 Park Rd, Ocean Springs — ~17 route miles past Pascagoula (use the +flex to set up a shorter Day 3)
spots.legalityNote: National Park Service campground, 52 sites, open year-round
spots.cyclistIntel: Reliable federal campground with hot showers; popular with coast-riding tourers as the Ocean Springs overnight
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; late-Sept mosquitoes on the bayou can be fierce — bring repellent

spots.name: McLeod Park Campground (Hancock County)
spots.priceNote: $35/night non-waterfront, $45 waterfront — all 120 sites are full-hookup county-park sites; tents accepted per camper listings (confirm when booking)
spots.locationNote: 8100 Texas Flat Rd on the Jourdan River near Kiln — ~4-5 mi from Diamondhead and near the inland detour toward Picayune
spots.legalityNote: Hancock County public park campground; camper-only bathhouse with hot showers, ADA-accessible
spots.cyclistIntel: The practical on-route choice for the Diamondhead/Kiln overnight — no backtrack, right at the top of your $35 ceiling. Older $23-26 riverside rates are gone since the 2020s rebuild
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round

spots.name: Buccaneer State Park (Royal Cay primitive area)
spots.priceNote: ~$20/night primitive tent (25 sites, restrooms within 100 yds); reservable developed tent sites $28; RV sites $28-40
spots.locationNote: 1150 S Beach Blvd, Waveland, on the beachfront — ~10-12 mi south of the Diamondhead endpoint; the route detours INLAND at Pass Christian toward Picayune, so this is an off-route coastal detour you'd have to un-ride next morning
spots.legalityNote: Mississippi state park; primitive tent area is first-come, developed sites via ReserveAmerica
spots.cyclistIntel: Was the standard MS-coast overnight on the old US-90 Southern Tier alignment; multiple bathhouses. Cheapest verified-legal bed of the day
spots.seasonalNote: Late Sept is shoulder season (Cruisin' the Coast crowds arrive early Oct); hurricane-watch closures possible

spots.name: Bay Hide Away RV Park & Campground
spots.priceNote: RV standard from $49; has only 5 tent sites 'available upon request' — tent rate unpublished, may be lower; call
spots.locationNote: 8360 Lakeshore Rd, Bay St. Louis/Lakeshore — well south of the inland detour (~14 mi off endpoint)
spots.legalityNote: Family-owned private campground; tents allowed on request
spots.cyclistIntel: Immaculate bathhouses per reviews; realistically a backup only given price and location
spots.seasonalNote: Open all year

spots.name: Berry Creek Cabins (tent/RV area)
spots.priceNote: Advertises tent camping + full-hookup RV sites with two bathhouses; nightly tent rate unpublished (est. $20-30) — call (985) 730-4395 before committing
spots.locationNote: 12101 George Jenkins Rd E (Bogalusa address), off the LA-21 corridor ~2-4 mi before Sun; near Bogue Chitto River tubing outfits
spots.legalityNote: Established private cabin/RV/tent operation on 7 acres in Washington Parish
spots.cyclistIntel: Only sleep-spot essentially ON route at the Sun endpoint (OSM tags it at mi 261); cabins from ~$100+ if storms roll in
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; office hours 9 AM-9 PM daily

spots.name: Bogue Chitto State Park
spots.priceNote: Improved W/E campsites $25-33+tax + $4.50 reservation fee; tent camping welcome on sites
spots.locationNote: 17049 State Park Blvd near Franklinton — ~13 hilly road miles NW of Sun via LA-10/LA-25; off-route detour both ways
spots.legalityNote: Louisiana state park; reservations via gooutdoorslouisiana.com or 877-226-7652
spots.cyclistIntel: Beautiful river-bluff park with 25 mi of trails, but the 26-mi round-trip detour makes it a fallback rather than a plan
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round

spots.name: Fontainebleau State Park
spots.priceNote: Unimproved tent sites in the LA $18-27+tax band (250+ unimproved sites, 33 designated tent sites, mostly first-come); improved W/E sites $28-42+tax + $4.50 reservation fee
spots.locationNote: Mandeville, on Lake Pontchartrain — ~20 route miles past Sun (lengthen the day, shorten tomorrow's run into NOLA)
spots.legalityNote: Louisiana state park, open year-round; tent camping is a core offering
spots.cyclistIntel: Sits directly on the Tammany Trace rail-trail — the North Shore cycling corridor — and is a frequent tourer camp; flush restrooms and showers at the tent areas
spots.seasonalNote: Fully reopened post-Ida; recent 2026 reviews confirm operational. Hurricane-season closures possible on tropical warnings

spots.name: India House Hostel
spots.priceNote: Dorm beds from ~$29-40 depending on night (Fri 9/25 will be the higher end); shared kitchen, courtyard; not camping but the cheapest legal in-city bed
spots.locationNote: 124 S Lopez St, Mid-City — ~2 mi from the downtown endpoint, right off Canal St streetcar
spots.legalityNote: Licensed backpacker hostel; bike storage usually available in the courtyard (confirm)
spots.cyclistIntel: Longtime budget standby for touring cyclists finishing/starting Gulf legs in NOLA; sociable, secure enough for a loaded bike
spots.seasonalNote: Book ahead for Friday nights

spots.name: Bayou Segnette State Park
spots.priceNote: $33+tax Fri-Sat ($30 Sun-Thu Apr-Sep) + $4.50 reservation fee; 98 improved W/E sites, tents welcome
spots.locationNote: Westwego on the West Bank — ~mi 344, 3.5 mi off route; from downtown take the Canal St-Algiers Point ferry (bikes OK, ~$2-3) then ~10 mi west
spots.legalityNote: Louisiana state park; standard legal camping closest to New Orleans
spots.cyclistIntel: THE stock answer to 'camping near NOLA' among tourers — ferry + West Bank ride is the accepted bike approach; wave pool and clean comfort stations
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; mosquitoes in late Sept

spots.name: New Orleans KOA Holiday (River Ridge)
spots.priceNote: Tent sites $60-98/night — far over budget; listed only because it's the one campground on the route's River Rd approach (mi 348)
spots.locationNote: 11129 Jefferson Hwy, River Ridge, near the Mississippi levee path ~13 mi upriver of downtown
spots.legalityNote: Commercial KOA; tents accepted
spots.cyclistIntel: Levee bike path runs nearby into the city; convenient but the price makes it a last resort
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round

spots.name: St. Bernard State Park
spots.priceNote: Improved W/E sites $20-28+tax (Fri 9/25 = $28) + $4.50 reservation fee; 50% off with America the Beautiful pass (out-of-state honored per LA reciprocity rules)
spots.locationNote: Braithwaite, ~18 mi SE of downtown along the Mississippi — overshoots the city on the East Bank/Chalmette side (Chalmette ferry option)
spots.legalityNote: Louisiana state park with partial-hookup RV and tent camping
spots.cyclistIntel: Quieter than Bayou Segnette but the approach roads (LA-39/LA-46) carry fast traffic; only worth it if continuing downriver next day
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; low-lying — closes on flood/tropical warnings

spots.name: Poche Plantation RV Resort
spots.priceNote: From $45/night, RVs ONLY — no tent camping allowed. Listed only so you don't route to it; cottages $119-139 if desperate.
spots.locationNote: 6554 LA-44 (River Road), Convent — EAST bank, ~9 mi behind Donaldsonville via the Sunshine Bridge.
spots.legalityNote: Private resort; explicitly no tents.
spots.cyclistIntel: Sometimes suggested to MRT riders but useless for a tent tourer.

spots.name: B & B RV Park
spots.priceNote: Nightly rate not published (weekly $150 ≈ $21/night; monthly $560). Long-term-oriented park; tent acceptance NOT verified — call before counting on it.
spots.locationNote: 100 Bellina Dr, Donaldsonville — in town, ~1 mi off the levee route. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established private RV park since 1980; laundromat and hookups confirmed, bathhouse/showers not confirmed.
spots.cyclistIntel: Only overnight facility inside Donaldsonville itself; no cyclist journal mentions found.

spots.name: Cajun Country Campground (Port Allen)
spots.priceNote: RV sites ~$40; tent sites offered per RV LIFE/Yelp listings but tent rate unpublished — estimate $25-30, confirm by phone. Phone-only reservations.
spots.locationNote: 4667 Rebelle Ln, Port Allen — west bank, just off the US-190 corridor near the Baton Rouge bridge crossing. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established private campground; bathhouse and laundry on site.
spots.cyclistIntel: Best-positioned legit tent campground between Donaldsonville and St. Francisville; sits basically on the corridor where the route crosses the Mississippi.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round.

spots.name: Farr Park RV Campground (BREC)
spots.priceNote: No-hookup/dry camping ~$10/night per recent reviews; full-hookup RV sites $35/night + tax. Tent use on grass reported by campers but confirm by phone.
spots.locationNote: 6402 River Road, Baton Rouge (EAST bank), directly on the Mississippi levee bike path ~10-12 mi south of the US-190 bridge bike crossing. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Public parish (BREC) recreation facility; phone reservations only, 14-night max.
spots.cyclistIntel: Dyrt reviews note a paved levee bike path runs directly from the campground toward the capital; popular with riders doing River Road. Bathhouse with 4 showers per side.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round.

spots.name: Tunica Hills WMA primitive campground (South Tract)
spots.priceNote: Free camping, but ages 16-59 must carry a LA hunting/fishing license or Wild Louisiana Stamp, plus free self-clearing permit at the kiosk.
spots.locationNote: Tent-only field off Parker Rd, South Tract, ~14 hilly mi NW of St. Francisville via US-61/LA-66/Old Tunica Rd. Off-route spur; coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Legal designated primitive camping area on LDWF land; porta-potties only, carry all water.
spots.cyclistIntel: Known as Louisiana's primitive-camping gem; the stamp requirement trips people up — buy online before the trip.
spots.seasonalNote: Late Sept: check LDWF for early hunting-season activity.

spots.name: Tunica Hills Campground (private)
spots.priceNote: Tent non-electric $20/night (2 people), electric $25; +$10 single-night surcharge +14% tax — expect ~$34 for one night. CASH ONLY.
spots.locationNote: 12112-12238 Parker Rd, ~15 mi NW of St. Francisville (same off-route spur as the WMA). Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established private campground; 20 sites with tent pads, hot-water showerhouse, pavilion with grill/microwave.
spots.cyclistIntel: Best legit tent camping in the St. Francisville area now that Green Acres is gone; small A-frame cabin $65 as a rain bailout.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; quiet hours 10pm.

spots.name: Peaceful Pines RV Park (formerly Green Acres Campground)
spots.priceNote: WARNING — OSM hint is stale for tenters: website states 'We do not offer tent camping at the RV park.' Nightly rates unpublished (monthly-focused). Do NOT plan on this or on 'Green Acres' (same place, renamed).
spots.locationNote: 11907 LA-965, 2.9 mi off route. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Explicitly no tents.
spots.cyclistIntel: Older journals mention Green Acres; that option effectively no longer exists for tents.

spots.name: Shelby J's RV Park
spots.priceNote: Rates not published; small locally-owned park, 30/50A + laundry. Tent acceptance unverified — ask; rural LA parks often say yes.
spots.locationNote: 14189 LA-10, ~3.5 mi west of US-61 — essentially ON the route toward the Audubon Bridge. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established RV park in West Feliciana Parish; amenities beyond hookups/laundry unconfirmed.
spots.cyclistIntel: Same owner also runs Tunica Trace RV Park (13155 Tunica Trace, LA-66).

spots.name: Jim's Camping Area (False River)
spots.priceNote: No-frills waterside campground; tents and RVs accepted per Campendium/Country Roads; rate unpublished — estimate $15-25, cash/cards.
spots.locationNote: 7913 Park St, north end of False River (New Roads/Ventress), ~11 route mi AHEAD of St. Francisville across the Audubon Bridge. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established commercial campground with bar & grill and boat launch; shower situation unverified.
spots.cyclistIntel: Matches the OSM 'Jim's Place mi 480.6' hint; hot food on site is a plus.

spots.name: Morganza church/community ask
spots.priceNote: Free with permission.
spots.locationNote: Tiny levee town (pop ~600) on LA-1 at the Morganza Spillway.
spots.legalityNote: Only with explicit permission from a church or town hall — standard rural-Louisiana courtesy stop, not verified for this town specifically.
spots.cyclistIntel: No specific journal record found for Morganza; treat as fallback if Maxey Care won't take a tent.

spots.name: Maxey Care RV Park and Campground
spots.priceNote: Rate unpublished — estimate $30-35 RV; tent acceptance unverified but it markets itself as 'RV Park and Campground' with a bathhouse — call.
spots.locationNote: 641 S LA-1, Morganza — 0.1 mi off the endpoint per OSM. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established private park; bathrooms with showers, coin laundry, 24-hr on-site managers confirmed. 2BR cabin available (sleeps 4) as bailout.
spots.cyclistIntel: The only facility at the Day 8 endpoint; covered pavilion useful in rain.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round.

spots.name: Yellow Bayou Civil War Memorial Park
spots.priceNote: Historically free/nominal camping for Southern Tier riders (the pre-2018 ST ran through Simmesport); CURRENT camping permission unverified — only picnic facilities are documented today. Call Avoyelles tourism (318) 964-2025 before relying on it.
spots.locationNote: 15602 LA-1, ~1.5 mi east of Simmesport near the Atchafalaya bridge; ~4 mi before the Day 9 endpoint. Coordinates approximate (HMDB marker).
spots.legalityNote: Public memorial park managed via Avoyelles Commission of Tourism; get explicit OK. Restroom/water status unknown — assume none and carry water.
spots.cyclistIntel: Multiple CGOAB ST journals (2007, 2014, 2017) overnight in Simmesport; Yellow Bayou was the traditional stop on the old ACA alignment.
spots.seasonalNote: Low, buggy ground near the bayou in late Sept.

spots.name: Simmesport church yard / town-hall ask
spots.priceNote: Free with permission. Leave a donation.
spots.locationNote: Simmesport town center, LA-1 — ~2.5 mi before the Day 9 endpoint.
spots.legalityNote: Ask at a church, the police department, or town hall; town saw regular cross-country cyclists for decades on the old ST alignment.
spots.cyclistIntel: CONFIRMED ACTIVE 2025: a town church sheltered a westbound group for two nights through a tornado warning - Sunday-school classrooms, fellowship hall, kitchen, plenty of toilets - and hosted a SEPARATE independent Southern Tier rider the same week. Ask at First Baptist or the Methodist church on arrival; town hall can point you. Earlier CGOAB journals (2007, 2014, 2017) also end in Simmesport, so this is a long tradition, not a one-off.

spots.name: Chicot State Park
spots.priceNote: Backcountry primitive sites $9-18/person/night first-come (6 sites); improved sites w/ water+electric $28-42 + tax, reserve online ($4.50 fee). $3/person day entrance.
spots.locationNote: 3469 Chicot Park Rd, ~7 mi N of Ville Platte — roughly 5 mi off the corridor, ~14 route mi BEFORE Mamou. Coordinates approximate (south entrance).
spots.legalityNote: Louisiana state park, open year-round; 198 improved sites with bathhouses.
spots.cyclistIntel: THE classic Louisiana ST/USBR90 camping stop — appears in decades of journals; stopping here makes Day 10 shorter and Day 11 (to DeRidder) ~14 mi longer.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; hot/humid with mosquitos late Sept — improved sites near the bathhouse recommended.

spots.name: Crooked Creek Recreation Area
spots.priceNote: From $23/night (Good Sam listing); tent sites reported $18-25, RV $25-35. Confirm by phone.
spots.locationNote: 1300 Sandy Beach Dr — on Crooked Creek Reservoir, ~14 mi NNW of Mamou via LA-13/LA-104. Off-route.
spots.legalityNote: Public parish recreation area, open all year; swimming beach, restrooms/showers, both drive-in and walk-in tent sites.
spots.cyclistIntel: Solid facilities but a real detour; only worth it if Chicot and the Mamou ask both fall through.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round.

spots.name: Mamou city ball field / church yard (police-arranged)
spots.priceNote: Free with permission from Mamou PD/town hall.
spots.locationNote: Mamou town center — the Day 10 endpoint.
spots.legalityNote: Only via explicit permission — precedent exists: a 2007 CGOAB Southern Tier journal records the police dispatcher setting tourers up at the local ball field.
spots.cyclistIntel: Mamou (Fred's Lounge town) is a long-standing ST waypoint; journals also warn the local RV campground felt sketchy — go through the police, not the RV lot.

spots.name: Big Oak RV Park
spots.priceNote: $20/day per Beauregard Tourist Commission — cheapest paid option in DeRidder. Tent acceptance unverified; 18 full-hookup sites, call.
spots.locationNote: 631 Hwy 171 S, southern edge of DeRidder, ~1-2 mi off the endpoint. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established RV park (laundry, wifi, pool); showers not confirmed.

spots.name: Happy Days RV Resort
spots.priceNote: Rate unpublished — typical DeRidder range $20-40; 30/50A full hookups, laundry. Tent policy unverified.
spots.locationNote: 2918 Hwy 190 W — on the westbound route out of DeRidder. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established private RV resort.

spots.name: Beauregard Parish Civic Center RV area
spots.priceNote: RV hookups $25/day, $100/week (parish tourism listing). Arena-grounds hookup pads; tents not addressed — ask when calling.
spots.locationNote: 5515 Hwy 190 West — directly ON the route heading west out of DeRidder toward Merryville. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Public parish facility with published overnight RV rates; tent policy unverified.
spots.seasonalNote: May be full during arena events.

spots.name: Merryville Museum cyclist camp
spots.priceNote: Donation basis — museum + cabin/showers are 'fee on a donation basis'; leave $10-20.
spots.locationNote: 628 N Railroad Ave, Merryville — just off US-190, ~18 route mi WEST (ahead) of DeRidder, ~7 mi before the Texas line. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Museum explicitly hosts cross-country cyclists: tent camping on the grounds or a raised stage area, plus a small cabin (fold-out couch, AC/heat, fridge, charging). Shower house and restrooms on site. Call/text ahead: (337) 340-1228 or (979) 864-0219.
spots.cyclistIntel: A famous lower-ST stop — 'proud host of guided cross country cyclists'; ACA groups camp here; Warm Showers-affiliated. Verified current via museum site and Beauregard tourism (tents only at the camp area, 2-night max).
spots.seasonalNote: Early Oct is prime hosting season.

spots.name: Merryville Museum cyclist camp (Burk's Cabin grounds)
spots.priceNote: Free/donation — museum members are 'proud hosts' of Southern Tier cyclists; small cabin (fold-out bed, AC, fridge, charging) or tent on grounds. Confirm donation amount when calling.
spots.locationNote: 628 N Railroad Ave, Merryville LA — ~20 route miles BEHIND the Kirbyville endpoint, before the Sabine crossing. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established cyclist hosting by the museum; fully sanctioned. Beauregard Tourism also lists a cyclists camping site at the Atakapa-Coushatta Trace Visitors Center, 703 N Bryan St.
spots.cyclistIntel: Well-known lower-Southern-Tier stop; hosts guided ACA groups and solo riders. Cafe in town praised in journals.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Kirbyville church yards (ask permission)
spots.priceNote: Free with permission; Southern Tier tradition — 'many riders stay at the church in Kirbyville' (Helder ST notes). Kirbyville Methodist, 105 W Main St; First Baptist, 105 N Barrow Ave.
spots.locationNote: In town, blocks from endpoint. Coordinates approximate (Methodist church).
spots.legalityNote: Legal only with explicit permission from church staff — call or knock before pitching. Do not set up unannounced.
spots.cyclistIntel: David Helder's Southern Tier notes say many riders overnight at the church in Kirbyville before the DeRidder leg; a Warm Showers host (Debbie) south of town also hosted riders in 2014 journals. Kirbyville has a small motel + groceries.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; October evenings mild.

spots.name: Magnolia Ridge Park (USACE, B.A. Steinhagen Lake)
spots.priceNote: $10/night tent non-electric; $18-20 electric. 50% off with federal Senior/Access pass.
spots.locationNote: Off US 190 near Woodville — roughly 28-30 miles NORTH of Kirbyville via Jasper, well outside the normal flex window. Only viable if deliberately rerouting via US 190. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established Corps of Engineers campground, 41 reservable sites, open year-round.
spots.cyclistIntel: Cheap and quiet, but the detour makes it impractical for the standard ACA routing — listed for completeness.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October availability is easy midweek.

spots.name: Red Cloud RV Park
spots.priceNote: Published nightly $50-60 all-inclusive appears to be the RV rate; tents accepted — call for tent price (may be less). Over budget if quoted RV rate.
spots.locationNote: 2351 US 96 N, Silsbee — essentially on-route (OSM pegs it at mile 733.2), ~13 mi before Kountze. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Commercial RV park with tent sites, bath house, laundry.
spots.cyclistIntel: On-route convenience is its only edge; mostly long-term residents per reviews.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Village Creek State Park (Creekside hike-in sites)
spots.priceNote: $10/night hike-in primitive site + $4/person daily entrance fee (TPWD entry is extra, per person 13+). Electric sites $16 + entry.
spots.locationNote: Lumberton, ~6 mi south of Silsbee off US 96 — leave the route around mile 737 before the final leg into Kountze (~10 mi east of the Kountze endpoint).
spots.legalityNote: TPWD state park; 15 hike-in sites with water nearby, restrooms with showers in park.
spots.cyclistIntel: The reliable legal-camping anchor for the Big Thicket day; several ST journals detour here rather than overnight in Kountze proper.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October midweek availability good.

spots.name: Indian Springs Camp
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not published — estimate $15-25; call to confirm.
spots.locationNote: 6106 Holland Cemetery Rd, Kountze — on Village Creek roughly 4-5 mi southeast of the Kountze endpoint. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Established private camp with dedicated tent and wilderness camping areas; baths/showers near tent area.
spots.cyclistIntel: Canoe/kayak outfitter camp on Village Creek; quiet on October weekdays.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; call ahead — office hours vary.

spots.name: Big Thicket National Preserve backcountry (Turkey Creek unit)
spots.priceNote: Free backcountry permit, issued in person at the visitor center same-day or up to 14 days ahead.
spots.locationNote: Visitor center at US 69/FM 420, ~7 mi north of Kountze (coordinates = visitor center; camp along Turkey Creek Trail 200 ft off trail). Off the westbound route direction.
spots.legalityNote: Legal ONLY with the free permit; camp 200+ ft from trails/roads/water (or on Village Creek sandbars within 25 ft of water); no campfires; pack out trash.
spots.cyclistIntel: Workable for a self-sufficient rider but logistically clunky: permit pickup requires reaching the visitor center during open hours, then hiking gear in. Carry all water.
spots.seasonalNote: Oct 1-Feb 28 hunting season limits camping to non-hunted areas — Turkey Creek, Village Creek Corridor, and Neches River Corridor units remain open year-round; Oct 3 is day 3 of that restriction.

spots.name: Big Thicket Hideaway Campground
spots.priceNote: RV sites from $35; tent rate unlisted — likely $20-30, call to confirm.
spots.locationNote: 5539 FM 420, Kountze — ~6 mi north of town near the Big Thicket visitor center. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Private campground advertising tent camping, showers, laundry, WiFi.
spots.cyclistIntel: Convenient pairing with a Big Thicket visitor-center stop; north-of-town location adds miles.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Lone Star Hiking Trail designated hiker camps (Big Woods/Magnolia sections)
spots.priceNote: Free; no permit needed.
spots.locationNote: Primitive designated camps along the LSHT near Double Lake/Big Creek Scenic Area, ~1-3 mi off route on foot paths. Coordinates approximate — use the LSHT Club map for exact camp locations.
spots.legalityNote: During hunting season (2025-26 policy: Sept 20-Jan 25; expect same window for 2026-27, covering Oct 4) SHNF camping is restricted to DESIGNATED sites — these hiker camps are the designated ones, so they stay legal. Wear orange.
spots.cyclistIntel: Fire ring/tent pad only; no water — tank up in Coldspring. Verify trail-section status with the ranger district: the 2024 flood closure order (expired June 1, 2026) had closed the whole LSHT and some sections may still be under repair.
spots.seasonalNote: Designated-camping-only period assumed in effect early Oct 2026; confirm 2026-27 dates at lonestartrail.org.

spots.name: Double Lake Recreation Area (Sam Houston NF)
spots.priceNote: $20/night tent non-electric single site (recreation.gov); day use $7/vehicle — walk/bike-in day use $1/person.
spots.locationNote: 1.4 mi off route at day's end (OSM mile 817.6), just south of Coldspring.
spots.legalityNote: Developed 1937 CCC campground, 43 sites (10 tent-only), flush toilets, bathhouse with concession; also first-come if sites open. No arrivals 10pm-6am.
spots.cyclistIntel: The obvious anchor for this day. IMPORTANT: it was on the 2024 flood closure list, but that order expired June 1, 2026 and the FS page now shows it OPEN (swim beach open since Apr 30) — still worth a confirming call since forest repairs are ongoing.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; verified open as of Aug 2026. Reserve on recreation.gov — October weekdays wide open.

spots.name: Kelly's Pond Campground (Sam Houston NF)
spots.priceNote: Camping is FREE (FS-confirmed); $5/person/day only if using the motorized trail system.
spots.locationNote: End of FSR 271, ~2.7 mi east of the day's endpoint (OSM hint). Gravel access road.
spots.legalityNote: Official FS campground: 8 primitive walk-in tent sites with tables, fire rings, lantern posts, vault toilets. FS page (Aug 2026): 'Dispersed Camping and Day Use are open.' Counts as a designated site during the hunting-season camping restriction.
spots.cyclistIntel: NO potable water — load up in Montgomery (3 mi). Popular with OHV riders on weekends, but Oct 5, 2026 is a Monday, so expect quiet. Cheapest legal bed on this whole segment.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; confirmed open post-flood-closure (order expired June 1, 2026).

spots.name: Little Lake Creek Wilderness / LSHT designated hiker camp
spots.priceNote: Free; no permit.
spots.locationNote: OSM shows a wilderness camp 0.9 mi off route near the endpoint (west side, LSHT western terminus area). Coordinates approximate — verify against LSHT Club map.
spots.legalityNote: Legal in Oct 2026 ONLY at designated hiker/hunter camps (hunting-season policy, ~Sept 20-Jan 25); random dispersed spots are off-limits in that window. Wear orange.
spots.cyclistIntel: Pure primitive — fire ring/tent pad at best, no water. Bikes not allowed on wilderness trail tread; you'd walk the bike or camp at a trailhead-adjacent designated site. Kelly's Pond is easier logistics for the same $0.
spots.seasonalNote: Confirm LSHT section status post-2024-flood repairs with the district office.

spots.name: Lake Conroe / Houston North KOA Holiday
spots.priceNote: ~$52/night average for premium tent sites (water, electric, fire pit); 20% weeknight discount Sun-Thu can pull it near $40. Over budget — fallback only.
spots.locationNote: 19785 TX-105 W, Montgomery — ~3.4 mi off route per OSM hint. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Commercial KOA; tents explicitly welcome.
spots.cyclistIntel: Hot showers, laundry, pool — a comfort splurge if the free NF options feel too rough after four camp nights.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Overlook Park & Marina (private)
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not published — estimate $25-35; call to confirm.
spots.locationNote: 505 Marina Rd, Brenham — east shore near the dam, ~3-4 mi off route. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Private marina campground with tent camping and a modern bathhouse (this is the 'Overlook Park' in OSM — it is NOT a free Corps day-use park).
spots.cyclistIntel: Nicest bathhouse on the lake per reviews; Brenham (~8 mi off route) remains the motel fallback.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Yegua Creek Park (USACE, Somerville Lake)
spots.priceNote: $20/night non-electric tent site; $26 tent site with 30A electric (2025 Corps rate sheet). Federal Senior/Access pass halves it to $10.
spots.locationNote: 12563 Yegua Creek Park Rd, Burton — south shore below the dam, ~3 mi off route per OSM hint (route mile ~940 between Gay Hill and Burton). Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Corps campground, open YEAR-ROUND, gated 6am-10pm; flush toilets, showers, water at sites.
spots.cyclistIntel: The classic cheap-with-showers Corps stop for this day; October weekday sites plentiful on recreation.gov (also bookable at 1-877-444-6777).
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round per Corps park list — no October closure.

spots.name: Rocky Creek Park (USACE, Somerville Lake)
spots.priceNote: Tent-only sites all have 20/30A electric + water — from $26/night (no cheaper non-electric tier here).
spots.locationNote: 10550 Rocky Creek Park Rd, Burton — south shore ~3 mi west of Yegua Creek, ~4-5 mi off route. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Corps campground, year-round, 192 sites incl. 35 tent-only; showers, restrooms.
spots.cyclistIntel: Backup if Yegua Creek is full (unlikely in October); slightly pricier since every site is electric.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Lake Somerville State Park - Nails Creek Unit
spots.priceNote: $12/night water-only site + $5/person daily entrance fee (TPWD entry extra). Electric $20 + entry.
spots.locationNote: Off FM 180 on the lake's southwest arm — ~8 mi north of the route near Burton (route mile ~944), ~15 total flex miles past Gay Hill.
spots.legalityNote: TPWD state park; restrooms with showers; primitive Trailway sites also available.
spots.cyclistIntel: Cheapest verified option on Somerville Lake, but the farthest pedal; only worth it if you're pushing past Gay Hill anyway.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; October availability good midweek.

spots.name: Buescher State Park (Oak Haven / Lakeview / primitive walk-in)
spots.priceNote: $15/night water-only tent site (Lakeview #41-60) or $15 primitive walk-in (#61-65, first-come) + $5/person daily entrance fee (TPWD entry extra). Electric (Oak Haven/Cozy Circle) $18 + entry.
spots.locationNote: Park camping loops are 0.1 mi off the route at the day's endpoint — the OSM 'Oak Haven', 'Cozy Circle', and 'Lakeview' camps ARE Buescher SP's camping areas.
spots.legalityNote: TPWD state park; restrooms with showers near Lakeview and the electric loops; primitive sites #61-65 are no-reservation first-come.
spots.cyclistIntel: Ends the day literally at the park gate; Smithville groceries/cafes 2 mi south. Reserve online for the water/electric sites, or roll in for a first-come primitive pad.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; October is prime season here but weekdays are fine.

spots.name: Vernon L. Richards Riverbend Park (City of Smithville)
spots.priceNote: $20/night (holiday weekends higher); all 19 paved sites have electricity, tables, grills, fire rings; tents allowed.
spots.locationNote: On TX-71 at the Colorado River on Smithville's north edge, ~1-2 mi off the endpoint. Coordinates approximate.
spots.legalityNote: Official city park camping; NO on-site office — reserve by phoning the City Recreation Center Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30 (Oct 7, 2026 is a Wednesday, so call that week). Showers not confirmed — restrooms only per city page.
spots.cyclistIntel: Cyclists and event campers use it regularly (hosts bike rallies); day use is free. Same price as Buescher but with electricity and no entry fee.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round.

spots.name: Bastrop State Park
spots.priceNote: $15/night water-only tent site (Deer Run, tents only) or $15 walk-in Creekside site + daily entrance fee (~$6/person — confirm). Electric $20, full hookup $25.
spots.locationNote: ~12 route miles PAST Smithville toward Bastrop (mile ~1016) — an overshoot option that shortens Day 18.
spots.legalityNote: TPWD state park; tent areas have water nearby, restrooms/showers in camp loops.
spots.cyclistIntel: Classic ST stop in the Lost Pines; note the historic Park Road 1C connector from Buescher to Bastrop is a beautiful but hilly ride.
spots.seasonalNote: Year-round; entrance fee amount not verified on the fetched page — budget ~$6/person.

spots.name: McKinney Falls State Park
spots.priceNote: $20/night 30-amp water+electric site ($24 for 50-amp) PLUS $6/person/day TPWD entrance fee — solo total ~$26
spots.locationNote: 5808 McKinney Falls Pkwy, SE Austin — ~7 mi from downtown endpoint, close to the inbound route from Bastrop, so easiest hit on the way IN
spots.legalityNote: Texas State Park; reserve at texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com
spots.cyclistIntel: Standard ST-rider choice for Austin — quiet, showers, and you skip downtown chaos; ride the 7 mi into town unloaded next morning
spots.seasonalNote: Thursday night in October usually available, but Austin parks book up around festival weekends — reserve ahead

spots.name: Emma Long Metropolitan Park (The Grove primitive sites)
spots.priceNote: $10/night primitive walk-in tent site (Grove or Bluff); utility sites $20-25. City of Austin park.
spots.locationNote: 1600 City Park Rd on Lake Austin — significantly off-route, ~12 road miles NW of the downtown/Zilker endpoint, hilly approach
spots.legalityNote: Official City of Austin campground; online reservation required (up to 180 days ahead)
spots.cyclistIntel: Cheapest legal tent spot in Austin metro, but the detour NW up City Park Rd is long and steep with a loaded bike — only worth it if you want two nights in Austin
spots.seasonalNote: Thu 8 Oct 2026; October weekends fill, weeknight usually fine but reserve

spots.name: Firehouse Hostel (downtown Austin)
spots.priceNote: Dorm beds from ~$29 (typically $29-45 by night); private rooms from ~$99. Indoor bed, not camping.
spots.locationNote: 605 Brazos St, downtown — ~0.7 mi from the Day 18 endpoint near Zilker/downtown
spots.legalityNote: Commercial hostel in Austin's 1885 fire station; 24-hour desk
spots.cyclistIntel: Largest hostel in Texas and the practical budget indoor option; secure your bike inside/ask staff
spots.seasonalNote: ACL Festival is traditionally the first two October weekends at Zilker — Oct 8-9 likely collides with fest weekend 2; dorm prices spike and sell out, book well ahead

spots.name: Pedernales Falls State Park
spots.priceNote: $20/night water+electric site (69 sites) PLUS $6/person/day entrance — solo ~$26. Hike-in primitive is $10 but sits 2 mi down a rough trail (impractical with a loaded touring bike).
spots.locationNote: ~9-10 road miles NE of Johnson City: turn off US-290 east of town onto FM 3232 / Park Rd 6026 before reaching JC, or backtrack from town
spots.legalityNote: Texas State Park; reserve online via Texas State Parks reservation system
spots.cyclistIntel: The only real budget camp near Johnson City now that the in-town RV parks have gone RV-only; showers, good facilities, swimming in the Pedernales
spots.seasonalNote: Friday night 9 Oct — Hill Country state parks fill on fall weekends; reserve as soon as dates firm

spots.name: Miller Creek RV Park
spots.priceNote: $52-62/night per aggregator listings — over budget, but tents are explicitly welcomed; call for a solo-tent rate, small parks often quote less
spots.locationNote: 5618 US-281 S, ~4-5 mi south of Johnson City (OSM pegs it at route mile 1123.4, on the line)
spots.legalityNote: Private commercial RV park that advertises tent camping
spots.cyclistIntel: Fallback if you don't want the Pedernales Falls detour; showers, laundry, store on site

spots.name: Kerrville-Schreiner Park
spots.priceNote: $25/night tent site (official city rate page); RV 30A water-only $35, full hookups $40-50. Some sources cite a $6/person entry fee on top — confirm when booking. City adds 3.5% surcharge on card payments (since Oct 2025).
spots.locationNote: 2385 Bandera Hwy (TX-173), on the Guadalupe ~3 mi SE of downtown Kerrville endpoint
spots.legalityNote: City of Kerrville park (517-acre former state park); tent areas in Riverside, Fox Run Loop, Fawn Hideaway
spots.cyclistIntel: THE classic Southern Tier stop in Kerrville — decades of ST journals and local bike-tour groups (about half of Easter Hill Country Tour riders) camp here; river swimming, showers, town services 3 mi away
spots.seasonalNote: Saturday night 10 Oct on a fall holiday weekend — reserve online ahead rather than rolling in

spots.name: Johnson Creek RV Resort & Park (Ingram)
spots.priceNote: Tent camping listed as available but nightly tent rate unpublished — estimate $30-45, call to confirm
spots.locationNote: Junction Hwy (TX-27/39 corridor) west of Ingram, ~7-8 route miles PAST Kerrville — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: Private RV resort that accepts tent campers per listings
spots.cyclistIntel: Useful if you want to bank miles past Kerrville toward Hunt; verify tent policy by phone first

spots.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area — primitive hike-in sites
spots.priceNote: $10/night + $6/person entrance (solo ~$16). CAUTION: sites are a 1-3.2 mi hike from parking on steep rough trails, no potable water, no fires — awkward to impossible with a loaded touring bike
spots.locationNote: Entrance on RM 187 north of Vanderpool; camping areas roughly 1.3-2.6 mi off the route line
spots.legalityNote: TPWD natural area; reservation via Texas State Parks system
spots.cyclistIntel: Cheapest on paper but you'd have to stash/push the bike down hiking trails — most riders take the developed loop or the private campground instead
spots.seasonalNote: Peak-crowd season starts in October; park closes entry when parking lots (250 cars) fill on color weekends

spots.name: Lost Maples RV and Camping (private)
spots.priceNote: $15/night primitive tent site (10 sites, no hookups); $24/night to pitch on an RV site with water+electric. 24-hour restrooms and showers.
spots.locationNote: 33557 RM 187 at Vanderpool, 0.1 mi off the route right at the day's endpoint
spots.legalityNote: Established private campground
spots.cyclistIntel: The zero-detour, no-lottery option at Vanderpool — showers included at half the SNA's developed-site cost; call ahead in October
spots.seasonalNote: Fall-color overflow from the SNA lands here — phone ahead for the holiday weekend

spots.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area — campsites with electricity
spots.priceNote: $20/night (30 sites, water+30A) + $6/person entrance — solo ~$26; showers in nearby restrooms
spots.locationNote: Developed loop near park HQ on RM 187, ~2-3 mi off route north of Vanderpool
spots.legalityNote: TPWD natural area; ReserveAmerica reservations
spots.cyclistIntel: Iconic overnight if you can get a site — maple canyon trails at your tent flap
spots.seasonalNote: CRITICAL: arrival is Sun 11 Oct 2026 — the Columbus Day long weekend and the front edge of leaf season. The 30 developed sites sell out far ahead on Oct/Nov weekends (bookable ~5 months out); reserve IMMEDIATELY or stalk cancellations. A Sunday night is your best shot vs Fri/Sat.

spots.name: Los Rios Campground
spots.priceNote: 10 tent sites (1-5 with water+electric, 6-10 primitive); rates only shown in their ResNexus booking engine — expect $20-35
spots.locationNote: 751 River Rd on the Nueces, ~4 route miles before Camp Wood (OSM mi 1273.9) — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: Established private campground (14 acres, cabins/tiny homes/RV/tent); men's & women's bathhouses
spots.cyclistIntel: Newer, well-reviewed river campground if the two in-town options don't pan out

spots.name: Wes Cooksey Park (Uvalde County)
spots.priceNote: ~$16/night camping (last verified rate, 2022) + $4/person day-use fee; current price unconfirmed — call (830) 597-3223
spots.locationNote: 33719 TX-55 on the Nueces at Camp Wood, 0.1 mi off route (OSM mi 1277.2) — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: County-run public park with RV and tent camping and river swimming; showers not confirmed
spots.cyclistIntel: Cheap public option right on the line entering Camp Wood; Camp Wood is a canonical ST overnight before the notoriously hard 36 westbound miles
spots.seasonalNote: Monday night 12 Oct (Columbus Day) — summer river crowds long gone, space near-certain

spots.name: Nueces River RV and Cabin Resort (formerly Big Oak River Camp)
spots.priceNote: Tent sites WITH water+electric; current rates not published online (legacy listings said ~$15) — book via bookings.rmscloud.com or call (830) 597-5280
spots.locationNote: 32598 TX-55, 0.3 mi off route at the day's endpoint (OSM mi 1278.3)
spots.legalityNote: Established private campground; note old domain bigoakrivercamp.com is dead — it rebranded
spots.cyclistIntel: This is the 'Big Oak River Camp' of countless ST journals — shaded oak/pecan tent sites a short walk from the Nueces, bathhouses, pool, camp store, laundry
spots.seasonalNote: Quiet mid-October weeknight

spots.name: Fort Clark Springs (Brackettville) — behind-route fallback
spots.priceNote: Tent camping listed at roughly $15-35/night, 2-person base +$1/extra person; COLD showers at tent area; RV full-hookup ~$40
spots.locationNote: Historic fort/member resort at Brackettville — ~30 route miles BEFORE the Day 23 endpoint, so it's a stop-short option, not a same-day one
spots.legalityNote: Private association resort that sells overnight camping to travelers; spring-fed pool
spots.cyclistIntel: Classic ST split-the-difference stop: if 68 mi Camp Wood→Laughlin is too big a day, sleep here and re-plan Del Rio as a short morning

spots.name: Hidden Valley RV Park (Del Rio)
spots.priceNote: Tent camping ~$20/night per directory listings (10% Good Sam discount cited); rate unverified — call ahead
spots.locationNote: Older shaded district of Del Rio, ~8 mi past the endpoint on the route through town (OSM mi 1354.7) — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: Private in-town RV park; laundromat on site
spots.cyclistIntel: In-town option if you want groceries, restaurants, and a real shower before the desert stretch

spots.name: Amistad NRA — 277 North Campground
spots.priceNote: $6-10/night NPS fee (50% off with Senior/Access pass); NO potable water, vault toilet, covered picnic table + grill
spots.locationNote: Off US-277 ~9 mi north of downtown Del Rio (a detour spur, not on the ST line) — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: National Park Service campground, first-come first-served, no reservations
spots.cyclistIntel: Dirt-cheap federal camping, but the 277 spur adds off-route miles — Governors Landing usually makes more sense for through-riders
spots.seasonalNote: Tue 13 Oct — FCFS is low-risk on a weekday in October

spots.name: Lonesome Dove RV Ranch
spots.priceNote: $22/night daily rate (weekly $135); tent policy NOT confirmed — sites are electric RV-style, phone first
spots.locationNote: US-90 W beyond Del Rio toward Amistad (OSM mi 1359.9) — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: Private RV park; treat tentsOk as unknown-leaning-no until confirmed by phone
spots.cyclistIntel: Only worth a call if Governors Landing is somehow full

spots.name: Amistad NRA — Governors Landing Campground
spots.priceNote: $6-10/night NPS fee; the ONLY Amistad campground with drinking water (shared spigots); vault toilets, no showers, no ground fires
spots.locationNote: Off US-90 W at the reservoir near Amistad Dam, ~12 route miles past the Day 23 endpoint / ~8 mi past downtown Del Rio — position approximate
spots.legalityNote: National Park Service campground, first-come first-served, 14-day max
spots.cyclistIntel: Long-standing ST bargain stop — banks miles toward Comstock and puts you lakeside; carry dinner/breakfast from Del Rio since there are no services
spots.seasonalNote: Weekday in October = sites open; sunset over the reservoir is the payoff

spots.name: Seminole Canyon State Park (Desert Vista / Roadrunner Flat primitive)
spots.priceNote: $10/night primitive site + $4/person daily entrance; sites with water $15 + $4
spots.locationNote: Park HQ off US 90, ~19 mi before Langtry; primitive areas a short ride inside the park
spots.legalityNote: TPWD state park - fully legal, reservable on Texas State Parks system
spots.cyclistIntel: The guaranteed option: potable water, restrooms with showers near the main loop, shade shelters at water sites. If Langtry feels sketchy on arrival day, shorten the day and stop here; next water is Langtry visitor center (8-5 only).
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; October is prime season - reserve the $15 water sites online, primitive usually has space

spots.name: Vashti Skiles Community Center (Langtry)
spots.priceNote: Free / suggested $2-5 donation via iron-ranger box
spots.locationNote: Torres Ave, right in Langtry, 2 blocks from the Judge Roy Bean Visitor Center; coordinates approximate
spots.legalityNote: Community-sanctioned overnight area (former school lot with donation box) - the long-running Langtry cyclist camp tradition continues here; no restrooms on site
spots.cyclistIntel: Southern Tier tradition of camping behind the Langtry community center is intact; Campendium reviews through Mar 2025 confirm overnights welcomed (quiet, level gravel, good 5G). Fill ALL bottles at the Judge Roy Bean Visitor Center (drinking water, flush restrooms, AC lobby, open 8-5 daily) BEFORE 5pm - there is no store, gas station, or other water in town. Local dogs bark at night per Mar 2025 review.
spots.seasonalNote: Visitor center was under construction in 2025 but lobby/restrooms stayed open 8-5 daily; call TxDOT center (432-291-3340) to confirm water access

spots.name: Terrell County Visitor Center / picnic area grounds
spots.priceNote: Free - Sanderson's famous cyclist camp
spots.locationNote: 108 E Oak St, downtown Sanderson, one block off US 90; coordinates approximate
spots.legalityNote: County-welcomed cyclist camping outside the community center/visitor center - a documented Southern Tier institution
spots.cyclistIntel: David Helder's Southern Tier notes: 'camp outside the community center; nice restrooms at the visitor center; water and WiFi always available.' Official county hours are now Wed-Sat 12-5 (Oct 15 2026 is a Thursday - open). Call ahead to confirm camping is still welcomed and where they want your tent.
spots.seasonalNote: Hours reduced vs the old 8-5; outdoor water spigot historically available even when closed - verify by phone

spots.name: Canyons RV Park
spots.priceNote: $7 tent + $3 shower per recent reviews - call to confirm current rate
spots.locationNote: US 90, east side of Sanderson, 0.1 mi off route
spots.legalityNote: Established commercial RV park, tents explicitly accepted
spots.cyclistIntel: Covered tenting pavilion with lights and electricity - huge in wind or rain. At $7+$3 shower this may beat the free option after 60 desert miles. Open year-round with full hookups, laundry, WiFi.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round

spots.name: Post Park (Fort Pena Colorado County Park)
spots.priceNote: Free county park camping
spots.locationNote: 5 mi south of Marathon at the south end of Avenue D / Post Rd - 5 mi OFF route each way
spots.legalityNote: Brewster County park; camping explicitly allowed on the east side of the spring-fed pond (pack out trash)
spots.cyclistIntel: Restrooms open 24/7, picnic tables, grills, cottonwood shade, spring pond (not potable - carry water from town). Lovely but adds 10 hilly bonus miles; only worth it if the in-town options fail.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round; occasional community events use the park

spots.name: La Loma del Chivo hostel
spots.priceNote: ~$20-25/night; long-standing tradition of cyclists' first night FREE if no paying guests - confirm when you call
spots.locationNote: 401 SW 6th St, a few blocks south of US 90 in Marathon; coordinates approximate - anyone in town can point you
spots.legalityNote: Private hostel property - fully legal, famously quirky (papercrete buildings, resident goats)
spots.cyclistIntel: THE legendary Southern Tier cyclist stop in Marathon - beds in eccentric handmade structures plus tent space, kitchen, showers. Active listings on Yelp (Dec 2025) and booking.com indicate still operating; reviews are polarizing (rustic/eccentric), so know what you're getting.
spots.seasonalNote: Appears operating as of late 2025 - call to verify before relying on it

spots.name: Marathon Motel & RV Park
spots.priceNote: $15/night tent per reviews - confirm by phone; motel/RV park confirms camping area on site
spots.locationNote: US 90 at the west end of Marathon, on route as you leave town westbound
spots.legalityNote: Established motel + RV park with dedicated tent camping behind the property
spots.cyclistIntel: Flat tent pads, picnic tables, clean restrooms/showers, laundry, and nightly stargazing with telescopes (certified dark-sky country). Reliable, easy, on route.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round

spots.name: Lost Alaskan RV Park (Alpine - 26 mi before Marfa)
spots.priceNote: ~$25-40; covered tent areas with electric; $40 full-site rate reported Oct 2024 - call for tent rate
spots.locationNote: 2401 N Hwy 118, Alpine - about 1.8 mi north of the US 90 route through Alpine
spots.legalityNote: Established commercial RV park with 8 dedicated covered tent sites (12x12 gravel pads, electric, picnic table)
spots.cyclistIntel: Use this if you want to split the day shorter and stay in Alpine (full grocery, bike shop, restaurants - the best resupply between Del Rio and El Paso). No online booking - phone only.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round

spots.name: Paisano Baptist Encampment
spots.priceNote: Unknown - historic church campground; fee/donation possible if they host you at all
spots.locationNote: 91872 US Hwy 90 at Paisano Pass, between Alpine and Marfa; coordinates approximate
spots.legalityNote: Private Baptist encampment grounds - ONLY with advance permission; no documented cyclist-hosting tradition found
spots.cyclistIntel: Century-old cowboy camp-meeting grounds with tabernacle and cabins, right on route at the pass. Summer meeting is July; grounds likely quiet in October. Contact via their website well ahead - do not just show up.
spots.seasonalNote: Main encampment event is in July; off-season access unverified

spots.name: Tumble In RV Park
spots.priceNote: $15/person tent (verified on official rates page); $25 for two
spots.locationNote: US 90 at the east edge of Marfa, ~1.5 mi before downtown - you pass it riding in; coordinates approximate
spots.legalityNote: Commercial RV park; tent camping first-come first-served (can pre-pay online but sites not reserved)
spots.cyclistIntel: Tent campers get access to all park facilities (restrooms/showers on site). Self-service vibe. Exposed and windy - stake well. NOTE: El Cosmico, the famous Marfa campground, has CLOSED its original site (relocating as 'El Cosmico 2.0') - do not plan on it.
spots.seasonalNote: Marfa fills up during events (Chinati Weekend is usually early-to-mid Oct) - arrive early to claim a tent spot

spots.name: Rancho Estrella Marfa (Hipcamp)
spots.priceNote: Rate not published in listing preview - check Hipcamp; area listings average $20-35
spots.locationNote: Edge of Marfa, ~0.5-1 mi walk to downtown; coordinates approximate
spots.legalityNote: Legal private-land camping booked through Hipcamp (tent sites around a 100-year-old adobe church)
spots.cyclistIntel: Toilet, potable water, showers, WiFi, picnic tables listed; currently bookable. Good backup if Tumble In is slammed for an event weekend.
spots.seasonalNote: Book ahead online

spots.name: Valentine School grounds (with permission)
spots.priceNote: Free with permission from school staff/principal
spots.locationNote: Valentine ISD school on US 90 in town (pop ~130); day marker mile 1647.2 sits ~4 mi NW of town - camp in town
spots.legalityNote: Permission-based only: a 2023 Southern Tier journal documents the principal allowing cyclists to camp on school grounds and use the bathrooms. Ask first - never set up unannounced at a school.
spots.cyclistIntel: Crazyguyonabike 2023 ('Pedaling Through the Southern Tier', Day 34 Van Horn to Valentine) camped here with staff permission and bathroom access. Arrive during school hours (before ~4pm) to ask; a weekend/holiday arrival makes this much harder. Oct 18 2026 is a SUNDAY - school will be closed, so call Valentine ISD the Friday before, or ask at the post office/any local.
spots.seasonalNote: School closed Sundays - arrange by phone in advance for an Oct 18 arrival

spots.name: Love Shaks (Airbnb vintage trailers)
spots.priceNote: ~$80-120/night estimated - over budget, but the only roofed option; owner has waived the 2-night minimum for passing cyclists
spots.locationNote: Vintage trailers in Valentine proper; find via Airbnb search 'Valentine TX'
spots.legalityNote: Legal short-term rental
spots.cyclistIntel: The 2023 CGOAB journal reports the Love Shaks owner waived the two-night minimum for cyclists passing through - message the host ahead explaining you're a Southern Tier rider.
spots.seasonalNote: Book several days ahead; inventory is tiny

spots.name: Van Horn RV Park (35 mi before, shortened-day option)
spots.priceNote: Tent rate not published; typical $20-25 - call 432-283-2728
spots.locationNote: 10 Kampers Lane, east side of Van Horn off the I-10 frontage (exact GPS from park website)
spots.legalityNote: Commercial RV park with 8 dedicated tent-only sites
spots.cyclistIntel: Tent sites have electric, water, picnic tables, BBQ grills; store, cafe (Penny's Cafe opens Oct 1 - perfect timing), laundry, restrooms and showers steps away. Van Horn is the last full-service town before El Paso; if the Valentine night went badly, stop short here and re-split the days.
spots.seasonalNote: Penny's Cafe on site operates Oct 1 - Apr 30

spots.name: Mountain View RV Park (Van Horn)
spots.priceNote: Estimated $15-25; large park listed as accepting tents - call to confirm
spots.locationNote: Van Horn, off Business I-10/Broadway; coordinates approximate - confirm location on arrival
spots.legalityNote: Commercial RV park listed as accepting tents (200 sites)
spots.cyclistIntel: Backup to Van Horn RV Park; Van Horn also has cheap motels ($45-60) if weather turns.
spots.seasonalNote: Open year-round

spots.name: Sierra Blanca Public Park
